  - heading "What a key can do" [level=2]
  - list:
    - code: get_policy_as_of
    - text: ": The policy as it stood on a business date: status, term, annual premium in force, state premium tax, policy fee, coverage limits and every endorsement applied by that date. Rebuilt from the policy's immutable events, not from a cache. Scoped to what this API key's user may see."
    - code: get_broker_statement
    - text: ": A published broker commission statement for one month: its lines, its totals (cash collected, premium collected, commission earned, clawbacks, net due), its content hash, its knowledge cutoff and its format version. Reads a stored run; nothing is recomputed. Scoped to what this API key's user may see."
    - code: list_reconciliation_breaks
    - text: ": The open breaks of the latest complete reconciliation run of each source (Stripe, and the LOCAL SIMULATOR claim payout rail): what each one is, how long it has been open, the two amounts and what it means. Also the clearing account balances, which should be zero once every flow has completed. Staff keys only."
    - code: run_reconciliation
    - text: ": Runs the reconciliation for a window ending now, against both sources (Stripe and the LOCAL SIMULATOR claim payout rail), and returns the run ids and the counts. It moves no money: it appends one run and its compared items. A run that could not fetch is stored as failed with its reason and compares nothing. Staff keys only."
    - code: request_claim_payment
    - text: ": Asks for a payment on a claim. This NEVER moves money: it writes the request and creates an approval request that a distinct human staff approver must decide (always when the key is held by an agent, rule 21; above the cumulative money-out threshold otherwise). A staff operator then sends it from the claim screen. Requires a staff_ops key."
  - heading "Never delegated to an agent" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: The same list is returned by
    - code: tools/list
    - text: under
    - code: policy
    - text: ", so an agent reading the surface sees it too."
  - list:
    - strong: approve or reject a money-out request
    - text: ": maker-checker exists so that a second HUMAN looks at money leaving. An agent deciding would be the same actor twice. There is no tool for it, the approval route accepts session cookies only, and the database refuses a decision by anyone whose role is not staff_approver."
    - strong: send a claim payment on the payout rail
    - text: ": this is money leaving. An agent may ask for one with request_claim_payment; a staff operator sends it from the claim screen, after an approver has said yes when it is above the threshold."
    - strong: issue or re-issue a refund at Stripe
    - text: ": money leaving again, with the same rule: a human cancels the policy and a human sends the refund."
    - strong: bind a policy
    - text: ": binding commits cover and creates the premium the customer owes. It also depends on the broker's KYB eligibility, which is checked at the moment of binding by a person who can see why it failed."
    - strong: cancel a policy
    - text: ": a cancellation stops cover and computes a refund. It is a customer decision carried out by a person."
    - strong: void a binding or record a correction
    - text: ": a correction rewrites what the ledger says happened (as reversals plus a re-book). Nobody should be able to correct history without a person naming the reason."
    - strong: run or publish a broker statement
    - text: ": a published statement is what we told a broker they were owed. Choosing its knowledge cutoff is a judgement call, so staff run it and agents read the result."
    - strong: change a broker's KYB status, or submit a verification
    - text: ": eligibility comes from the provider's own decision and from the documents a broker really signed. Nothing an agent asserts may move it."
    - strong: create, revoke or read an MCP API key
    - text: ": an agent that could mint keys could grant itself another user's visibility. Keys are created and revoked by staff on /ops/mcp-keys, or by a script run by a person."
    - strong: replay a webhook, or write anything into the ledger directly
    - text: ": journal entries are posted by the business operations that cause them. There is no general write tool, and the runtime database role holds SELECT and INSERT only on every money table."
- contentinfo: Corgi · Policy administration

  - heading "What a key can do" [level=2]
  - list:
    - code: get_policy_as_of
    - text: ": The policy as it stood on a business date: status, term, annual premium in force, state premium tax, policy fee, coverage limits and every endorsement applied by that date. Rebuilt from the policy's immutable events, not from a cache. Scoped to what this API key's user may see."
    - code: get_broker_statement
    - text: ": A published broker commission statement for one month: its lines, its totals (cash collected, premium collected, commission earned, clawbacks, net due), its content hash, its knowledge cutoff and its format version. Reads a stored run; nothing is recomputed. Scoped to what this API key's user may see."
    - code: list_reconciliation_breaks
    - text: ": The open breaks of the latest complete reconciliation run of each source (Stripe, and the LOCAL SIMULATOR claim payout rail): what each one is, how long it has been open, the two amounts and what it means. Also the clearing account balances, which should be zero once every flow has completed. Staff keys only."
    - code: run_reconciliation
    - text: ": Runs the reconciliation for a window ending now, against both sources (Stripe and the LOCAL SIMULATOR claim payout rail), and returns the run ids and the counts. It moves no money: it appends one run and its compared items. A run that could not fetch is stored as failed with its reason and compares nothing. Staff keys only."
    - code: request_claim_payment
    - text: ": Asks for a payment on a claim. This NEVER moves money: it writes the request and creates an approval request that a distinct human staff approver must decide (always when the key is held by an agent, rule 21; above the cumulative money-out threshold otherwise). A staff operator then sends it from the claim screen. Requires a staff_ops key."
  - heading "Never delegated to an agent" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: The same list is returned by
    - code: tools/list
    - text: under
    - code: policy
    - text: ", so an agent reading the surface sees it too."
  - list:
    - strong: approve or reject a money-out request
    - text: ": maker-checker exists so that a second HUMAN looks at money leaving. An agent deciding would be the same actor twice. There is no tool for it, the approval route accepts session cookies only, and the database refuses a decision by anyone whose role is not staff_approver."
    - strong: send a claim payment on the payout rail
    - text: ": this is money leaving. An agent may ask for one with request_claim_payment; a staff operator sends it from the claim screen, after an approver has said yes when it is above the threshold."
    - strong: issue or re-issue a refund at Stripe
    - text: ": money leaving again, with the same rule: a human cancels the policy and a human sends the refund."
    - strong: bind a policy
    - text: ": binding commits cover and creates the premium the customer owes. It also depends on the broker's KYB eligibility, which is checked at the moment of binding by a person who can see why it failed."
    - strong: cancel a policy
    - text: ": a cancellation stops cover and computes a refund. It is a customer decision carried out by a person."
    - strong: void a binding or record a correction
    - text: ": a correction rewrites what the ledger says happened (as reversals plus a re-book). Nobody should be able to correct history without a person naming the reason."
    - strong: run or publish a broker statement
    - text: ": a published statement is what we told a broker they were owed. Choosing its knowledge cutoff is a judgement call, so staff run it and agents read the result."
    - strong: change a broker's KYB status, or submit a verification
    - text: ": eligibility comes from the provider's own decision and from the documents a broker really signed. Nothing an agent asserts may move it."
    - strong: create, revoke or read an MCP API key
    - text: ": an agent that could mint keys could grant itself another user's visibility. Keys are created and revoked by staff on /ops/mcp-keys, or by a script run by a person."
    - strong: replay a webhook, or write anything into the ledger directly
    - text: ": journal entries are posted by the business operations that cause them. There is no general write tool, and the runtime database role holds SELECT and INSERT only on every money table."

    - text: The two collected figures
  - paragraph: "The two collected figures are the same money read twice: the cash line is what the customers paid, premium plus state premium tax plus policy fee, and the premium line is the part of it commission is earned on. Both come from the journal: the cash from the collection entries, the premium from the entries that wrote it under the same payment. Commission is the premium times the broker's rate, rounded down, and never touches tax or fee. Refunds are not netted into these two figures; they are on their own lines, next to the clawback each one produced."

  - paragraph: "The two collected figures are the same money read twice: the cash line is what the customers paid, premium plus state premium tax plus policy fee, and the premium line is the part of it commission is earned on. Both come from the journal: the cash from the collection entries, the premium from the entries that wrote it under the same payment. Commission is the premium times the broker's rate, rounded down, and never touches tax or fee. Refunds are not netted into these two figures; they are on their own lines, next to the clawback each one produced."

    - generic "Reproducing this statement":

    - paragraph: "Running 2026-09 again for Redwood Commercial Brokers with the knowledge cutoff above reads the same journal entries and produces the same content hash, because a journal row can never change and its recording time is stamped by the database. One case does not reproduce, and it is the reason a provisional run says so: an entry whose database transaction started before that cutoff and committed after this run had read the ledger is absent here and present in a later run with the same cutoff. Once the month is closed and quiet, which is what a monthly statement is for, it cannot happen."
    - generic "Provisional":
      - text: Provisional
    - paragraph: This run was produced before 2026-09 was over, so more money could still be booked into it. It stays exactly as it is; the run made after the month ends is the next revision and the definitive one.
    - generic "Format changed":
      - text: Format changed
    - paragraph: "The statement format changed between revision 2 (v1) and this one (v2): the two documents hash different texts, so they cannot be compared by hash. The journal entries still can be, and they are."
    - generic "Ties to the ledger":
      - text: Ties to the ledger
    - paragraph: The net due printed on the statement is compared, live, with the movement of this broker's commission payable account in the journal, read again with the same month and the same knowledge cutoff by a second, much smaller query. Two independent reads of the same ledger have to agree to the cent, and the page says so either way rather than assuming it.

  - paragraph: "The two collected figures are the same money read twice: the cash line is what the customers paid, premium plus state premium tax plus policy fee, and the premium line is the part of it commission is earned on. Once the month is closed and quiet, which is what a monthly statement is for, it cannot happen."
